```markdown
# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen quarter range, downloaded and kept | R1; §2.1, §4.2 | A | 1 | About 2 SEC requests per quarter (listing + `master.idx`, §4.2), so request time is trivial at 3 req/s (§4.8). Bytes are measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | R2; §4.2 | A | 2 | About 63 daily files per quarter (business days) plus listings. Under a minute per quarter at 3 req/s. Bytes are measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | A validated, deduplicated filing-index table in Parquet built from those indexes | R3; §4.4, §4.5, §4.6 | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipelines running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor | R4; §4.1, §4.7, §4.9 | A | 4 | No estimate until the sizes, region and retention in §4.8 are chosen. Measured by the Stage 7 smoke test |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | Partner time only |
| O6 | Original bytes kept, so a parser change reprocesses without re-downloading | R6; §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage equals raw bytes per snapshot, measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read periodically, with corrections folded in and history kept | R7; §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | About 2 requests per supported quarter per weekly run (§4.8) |
| O8 | All SEC traffic under one shared request budget, however many workers run | R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | Partner time only |
| O9 | Readers resolving each quarter through one versioned active pointer, never a partial set | R9; §4.5, §4.6 | A | 9 | Partner time only |
| O10 | No filing leaving the active catalog without approval tied to the exact source hash | R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Partner time per gated candidate |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target held as validated, reviewable configuration | R11; §4.8, §5 | A | 11 | Partner time only |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly backfill to Parquet
      Objective: Download a small real range of quarterly indexes and produce a validated filing-index Parquet table locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: the quarter range and SEC User-Agent identity, recorded by your partner (§7 step 1)
      Produces: a downloader and parser in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the raw `master.idx` bytes for every quarter in the chosen range are on disk, with SHA-256 values. O3 — a Parquet table with the §4.5 row contract has no duplicate `(cik, archive_path)` keys, and malformed input is refused. The findings file records the measured bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and observed request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: daily ingestion → Stage 2; source manifest and replay identities → Stage 3; generations and active pointer → Stage 4; reconciliation → Stage 5; shared lease budget and config validation → Stage 6; Azure, monitoring and alerts → Stage 7; golden fixtures across the full range, and scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from a handoff date, catching up across missed runs and quarter boundaries.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader and parser
      Produces: daily discovery and catch-up merged into the Stage 1 table, with baseline overlap deduplicated
      Exit: O2 — a run from a past handoff date ingests every listed daily file through the present. A failed listing does not advance the boundary. A run with nothing new reports `no_new_sources`.
      Leaves out: source manifest → Stage 3; scheduling → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Shared commands, source manifest and replay
      Objective: Run backfill and daily ingestion through the shared discover/collect/transform/publish commands over durable worksets and a source manifest.
      Outcomes: O5, O6
      Consumes: Stages 1–2
      Produces: the §4.5 source manifest records, content-addressed raw storage and the CLI commands
      Exit: O5 — backfill and daily runs differ only in source selection. O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds the output from stored bytes with zero SEC requests, and resumes partial work without losing completed units.
      Leaves out: Table Storage backing → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Quarter generations and active pointer
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3
      Produces: generation writes, manifests, change reports and the pointer protocol (§4.6)
      Exit: O9 — under injected crashes before files finish, before the pointer update and after it, readers see only complete generations. Competing publishers lose no update.
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate → Stage 5
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Reconciliation with withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources, publish safe changes, and gate withdrawals on hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stages 3–4
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow and approval records
      Exit: O7 — additions and field updates publish with recorded changes, and unchanged hashes skip work. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval naming its exact hash. Open-quarter absence withdraws nothing, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key.
      Leaves out: weekly schedule → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Shared request budget and validated configuration
      Objective: Put every SEC request under one lease-coordinated budget, and validate configuration before any I/O.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stages 1–5
      Produces: the request lease, retry and halt policy (§4.3, §5) and the typed `conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml`
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors never overlap as request issuers, and retries count toward the budget. O11 — each §5 configuration error is refused before external I/O.
      Leaves out: Storage-backed lease on Azure → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment with triggers disabled
      Objective: Deploy the shared worker, ADF pipelines, storage, identities and alerts to an isolated environment, then run the smoke test.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; the ADR and spec accepted (§7 step 1)
      Produces: `infra/azure/sec-edgar-ingest/`, `docs/runbooks/`, and the smoke-test record (§7 steps 3–5)
      Exit: O4 — ADF starts and polls a job to a terminal outcome. The integration tests and fault injection pass. The live smoke test records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate. Replay with SEC access disabled gives unchanged output.
      Leaves out: trigger enablement → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the full backfill and daily catch-up, then the manual reconciliation, then enable the schedules (§7 Phase 2).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 at production standard
      Consumes: Stage 7
      Produces: a release record with image and configuration versions and the active generations
      Exit: O1 — every requested quarter is published, or the incomplete range is recorded explicitly, with golden fixtures covering the range's formats (§4.6). O2 — the daily trigger runs on schedule and its durable reports match. O7 — a scheduled reconciliation runs and any gated candidate is resolved.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

Run SKILL.md §6 over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict. Every spec requirement R1–R11 is cited by an outcome's `Spec` cell, so none starts unmet.
```

**Message:** The roadmap is written: eight stages in Track A. The order follows your ranking except for three changes. O3 joins O1 so Stage 1 yields a usable table. O4 (Azure) moves to Stage 7 because it deploys code built in Stages 1–6. O9 (publication) comes before O7/O10 because the withdrawal gate sits in the publish step.
